question: What is the required size of the Olympic swimming pool?
solution:
The correct answer is __**50 m × 25 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Swimming pool:

__
 
• ​The swimming pool standard size is :

 
 
• 50m length
 
• 25m width
 
 
 
• It must have 10 lanes.
 
• The width of the lane should be 2.50m.
 
• The range of the temperature should be 25-28o C.
 
• The lighting level should be more den 3000 lux.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Swimming:
 
• Swimming is an individual or team racing sport that requires the use of one's entire body to move through the water.
 
• The sport takes place in pools or open water (e.g., in a sea or lake).
 
• Competitive swimming is one of the most popular Olympic sports, with varied distance events.
 
• It has 4 styles of swimming.

 

 
• Strokes in swimming:

 
 
• Freestyle
 
• Backstroke
 
• Butterfly
 
• Breaststroke.
 
• Swimming Federation of India:
 
• The Swimming Federation of India (SFI) is the national governing body for aquatic sports in India.
 
• Legally, it is a non-profit association registered under the West Bengal Societies Registration Act, 1861.
 
• The federation holds elections for its office bearers every four years.
 
• The SFI currently oversees competition in the sports of swimming, masters swimming, synchronized swimming, diving, high diving, and water polo.
 
• It is affiliated with FINA, and the Asia Swimming Federation (AASF).
 
• The SFI was formed by the merger of the National Swimming Association (NSA) and the Indian Swimming Federation (ISF) in 1948.
